In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Commentary on Surah al-Jumu'ah (The Congregation)

It is Medinan according to all scholars. Some of them mentioned that it is Meccan, but this is not correct.

His Exalted saying: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾. The meaning of tasbih (glorification, i.e., declaring Allah far above everything unfitting for Him) has already been explained; it is the declaration of the Lord's transcendence above everything that does not befit Him. It is also said: tasbih for Allah is the remembrance of Allah. Al-Qaffal al-Shashi mentioned that the meaning of the glorification of inanimate things is what has been placed in them of signs of their having been originated, and that they have a Maker and a Creator. This is not correct, and we have previously mentioned what the people of the Sunnah say about it.

And His saying: ﴿the Sovereign, the Most Holy﴾, i.e., the One pure from every defect and blemish.

And His saying: ﴿the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾, i.e., the Victorious in His command, the Just in His action.

The Exalted said: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered (al-ummiyyin) a Messenger from among themselves﴾. Mansur narrated from Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i): the ummi is the one who neither writes nor reads.

Ibn Umar narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "We are an unlettered (ummiyya) nation; we do not write nor calculate the month like this, like this, and like this," and he gestured with his ten fingers, and in the third instance he held down his thumb.

It is also said: the ummi is so named in reference to the state in which his mother bore him (i.e., he remains as he was born). It is also said: he was named ummi because he is the original state of a nation's natural disposition, and writing is only acquired through learning. Some have said: the Quraysh were called ummiyyin in reference to Umm al-Qura, which is [Makkah]. If someone says: not every Quraysh was unlettered, yet He said ﴿among the unlettered﴾? The answer: Allah named them unlettered in consideration of the majority of their condition, for writing was rare among them. The Arabs used to call one who knew writing, swimming and archery a "poet" (shā'ir) as a mark of perfection.

Ibn Abbas said: Quraysh learned writing from the people of al-Hira, and the people of al-Hira learned it from the people of al-Anbar.

The wisdom in the Messenger being unlettered is the removal of the accusation against him of learning the reports of the earlier peoples and studying them from their books. It is also said: so that he would conform to his description in the books of the earlier peoples.

His saying ﴿He recites to them His verses﴾ means: the Qur'an.

His saying ﴿and teaches them the Book﴾ means: the Book of Allah. Ibn Abbas said: it is writing with the pen, for writing became widespread among Quraysh and the rest of the Arabs after the Messenger of Allah, and this agrees with the saying of the Exalted: ﴿He taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know﴾.

His saying ﴿and the wisdom﴾ means: the Sunnah. It is also said: understanding of the religion.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed they were before in manifest error﴾ means: in clear error, away from the truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 62, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And others among them﴾. Al-Azhari said: it is in the place of the genitive (khafd), meaning: He was sent to the unlettered ones (al-ummiyyin) and to others.

And His saying: ﴿who have not yet joined them﴾, meaning: they have not yet joined them, but they will join them. It is also said regarding His saying ﴿and others﴾, meaning: He teaches them the Book and the wisdom, and He teaches others. Al-Naqqash narrated it.

The opinions differed concerning who is meant by "the others." ʿIkrimah said: they are the Successors (al-tabi'un). Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: they are the non-Arabs (al-ʿajam). The one who holds this view relies on what Abu Hurayra narrated: that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse and pointed to Salman, and said: "If the religion were suspended at the Pleiades, men from this people would attain it," meaning: the non-Arabs. Al-Dahhak said: it is everyone who believes and does righteous deeds until the Day of Resurrection.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ — we have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 62, verse 4:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills﴾. That is, prophethood. It is also said: it refers to what was mentioned earlier, namely the teaching of the Book and the wisdom.

As for His words, ﴿And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾, it is clear. And it has been related in a report (khabar) that the poor complained to the Prophet and said: "The people of wealth have taken the rewards." So the Messenger directed them to glorification (tasbih), declaration of God's oneness (tahlil), and various kinds of remembrance (dhikr). The wealthy heard of this and began saying the same as the poor. The poor then came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned this to him. So he recited this verse, and it is His words: ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty﴾. And this is a well-known report.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 62, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The likeness of those who were entrusted with the Torah﴾, meaning: those who were entrusted with upholding it (wa-istiʿmaluhā, "and acting upon it"). This is from al-hamālah (guarantee, undertaking responsibility), not from al-ḥaml (carrying); that is, they undertook to uphold it and to act by what is in it.

And His saying: ﴿then they did not carry it﴾, meaning: they neglected it and did not act by what is in it. ﴿Are like the donkey which carries books⁠﴾. Ibn Masʿud recited: "like a donkey carrying books" (kamathali ḥimārin yaḥmilu asfāran). Al-asfār is the plural of safar, and the safar is the book. So He made the disbelievers, when they neglected the Book of God and did not act by what is in it, like donkeys that carry books and do not know what is in them.

And His saying: ﴿Wretched is the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God﴾, meaning: wretched is the likeness, the likeness of the people who denied the signs of God. And His saying: ﴿God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 62, verse 6:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: O you who have become Jews, if you claim that you are the friends of Allah to the exclusion of other people⦆ (the Jews). It is mentioned in some tafsirs that the Jews of Madinah sent to the Jews of Khaybar to ask them about the Prophet. The Jews of Khaybar wrote back to the Jews of Madinah saying: "We do not know of a prophet who will emerge from the Arabs, and this man wants to humiliate you and diminish your standing. You are the friends and beloved of Allah, so do not follow him." Then Allah, Exalted is He, revealed this verse.

His saying: ﴿if you claim that you are the friends of Allah to the exclusion of other people﴾ refers to what we have just mentioned.

His saying: ﴿then wish for death, if you are truthful﴾ means: if you are truthful that you are the friends of Allah. For if you die, you will reach the honour of Allah and His Garden according to your claim, so wish for it in order that you may attain it. In most tafsirs it is stated that this verse is a miracle of the Messenger, for Allah had decreed that if they wished for death they would die at that very moment. So none of them wished for death. In their restraint from wishing for it, despite their eagerness to demonstrate the Messenger's lie, and in their knowledge that if they wished for it they would die, there is proof of the Messenger's truthfulness.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forward﴾. He informed that they will not wish for it, and none of them wished for it.

And His saying: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: of their wronging of themselves by concealing the description of the Messenger (ﷺ) in their scriptures.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 62, verse 8:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Indeed, the death from which you flee - indeed, it will meet you﴾. In the verse is evidence that they would die even if they had wished (for it); and they had not wished to flee from death.

And His words: ﴿indeed, it will meet you﴾, meaning: death will meet you.

And His words: ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, meaning: the Knower of what is manifest and what is hidden.

And His words: ﴿and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾, meaning: of what you have done.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 62, verse 9:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when the call is proclaimed for prayer on the day of Friday (jumu'ah)...﴾ That is: for the Friday prayer on the day of Friday. The day is called jumu'ah because on this day the creation of Adam was gathered (jama'a). Some have also narrated this as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report from the Prophet (ﷺ).

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿then hasten (fas'aw) to the remembrance of Allah﴾. ʿUmar, Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn al-Zubayr read: "then proceed (famdu) to the remembrance of Allah." Ibn Mas'ud said: "If I were to recite 'fas'aw ila dhikr Allah', I would run until my cloak fell off." The well-known reading is "fas'aw." It has been narrated from some of the Successors (tabi'un) that they used to run. Thabit al-Bunani said: "I was with Anas ibn Malik when the call to the Friday prayer was proclaimed, and he said: 'Get up, let us hasten (nas'a).'"

The correct view is that sa'y here means action and doing. This was said by Mujahid and others, and it is related from al-Shafi'i, who cited His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that man has only what he strives for (sa'a)﴾, meaning only what he does, and likewise His saying: ﴿Indeed, your efforts (sa'yakum) are diverse﴾, and similar verses. The poet said:

(I strive for the sake of the camels of Banu Malik... every person is a striver in his own affair.)

So sa'y here means action and conduct. It is narrated from al-Hasan and Qatadah that what is meant by His saying ﴿fas'aw﴾ is the intention in the heart and the resolve toward it. ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Samit said: "I was walking with Abu Dhar to the Friday prayer when we heard the call to prayer, so I quickened my pace, and he seized me by a pull and said: 'Are we not hastening (nas'a)?'"

His saying: ﴿to the remembrance of Allah﴾ has two interpretations: the first is that it refers to the khutbah (sermon), and the second is that it refers to the prayer. The second is the more sound.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and leave off trade (al-bay')﴾, that is: and abandon trade. It is said that what is meant is when the time of prayer has entered, even if the call has not yet been given for it; and it is said that it is after hearing the call. The first is better. Whoever holds the second view says: the call is the adhan when the imam sits on the minbar, which was the practice in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). As for the first adhan, ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him) introduced it when the people became numerous. What is meant by His saying ﴿and leave off trade﴾ is trade and purchase and everything that distracts from the Friday prayer.

The scholars differed over whether, if one does sell, that sale is valid. Most of them held that the sale is valid and the prohibition is disapproval (karahah). Malik and Ahmad held that the sale is not valid at all. Some have related from Malik that he retracted from prohibition to disapproval. The first view is preferable, because Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is better for you, if you knew﴾; He made leaving trade better, which points to disapproval of the act rather than prohibition. Also, the prohibition of the contract is for the sake of distraction from the Friday prayer, not for the contract's own substance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 62, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then when the prayer is concluded﴾, i.e., when it has been finished.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿then disperse in the land and seek of the bounty of Allah﴾. This is a command of recommendation (amr nadb), not a command of obligation and requirement (amr hatm wa-ijab), like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾. It is reported from Ibn Muhayriz that he said: "I like that I should have some need after the Friday prayer, so that I turn to it and seek of the bounty of Allah through it." It is reported from Abdullah [ibn] Busr that he used to leave the mosque when he had prayed the Friday prayer, then he would return and sit until he prayed the afternoon prayer (al-'asr). And in some reports from the Prophet, regarding the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿then disperse in the land and seek of the bounty of Allah﴾, he said: "It is not the seeking of worldly gain; rather it is visiting a sick person, or attending a funeral, or visiting a brother for the sake of Allah." And the report is gharib (rare, weakly transmitted).

As for His saying: ﴿And remember Allah much that you may succeed﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 62, verse 11:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it﴾. The occasion of revelation of this verse is that the Messenger of Allah was on the minbar delivering a sermon, and the people of Madinah had been struck by high prices and famine. A caravan (ʿayr) carrying food arrived, and it is said that it belonged to Dihya ibn Khalifa al-Kalbi. They stopped at the Ahjar al-Zayt (the Olive Stones) and struck the drum to let the people know. The Muslims heard this in the mosque and went out to it, and the Prophet remained with twelve men, among them Abu Bakr and ʿUmar. Al-Bukhari transmitted a report about this and mentioned this number. It is also said that there were eight men, but the first (number) is more sound. Then Allah the Most High revealed this verse.

"Trade" is well known; it is trade in food and procuring it. "Diversion" is the drum; this is the view of Mujahid. It is also said that it refers to the flutes (mazamir). The Ansar used to make such sounds when they escorted a woman to her husband, and this is like the tambourine (duff), the drum and what resembles them. According to this view, the Muslims heard its sound in the market, and they were escorting a woman, so they went to it. The first is the well-known and established view.

His words: ﴿And they left you standing﴾, because he was delivering the sermon. This indicates that the Sunnah is to deliver the sermon standing. The first to deliver the sermon sitting was Muʿawiya, and Marwan followed him in this. The Sunnah is what we have explained.

If someone asks: how did He say ﴿they rush off to it﴾ when two causes were mentioned, trade and diversion, and did not say "they rush off to them (both)"? The answer is that its meaning is: when they see a trade, they rush off to it, and when they see a diversion, they rush off to it; so one of them was sufficient in place of the other. We have mentioned before that the Arabs may mention two things and return the pronoun to one of them, while both are meant. The poet said:
"We are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have,
though the opinions differ."

It is also said that there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse, and its meaning is: when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush off to it. The infidad (rushing away) is going off quickly.

His words: ﴿Say: What is with Allah is better than diversion and than trade﴾, meaning: the remembrance of Allah the Most High and occupation with the prayer are better than diversion and trade. His words: ﴿And Allah is the best of providers﴾. Al-Zajjaj said its meaning is: He provides for you and does not withhold it from you, so do not busy yourselves with seeking it to the neglect of the prayer and the remembrance of Allah. It is also said: provision is given to both the righteous and the wicked. Al-Husayn al-Basri narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, when the people hurried away to the caravan and he remained with twelve men: "Had the last of them joined the first, the valley would have blazed with fire upon them."

Many reports have come concerning the excellence of Friday and its reward, among them: what Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab narrated from Jabir, from ʿAbd Allah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O people, repent to your Lord before you die, hasten to righteous deeds before you are preoccupied, and connect what is between you and your Lord by much remembrance of Him and by charity in secret and in public, and you will be victorious, be made whole and be provided for. Know that Allah the Most High has made Friday obligatory upon you in this place of mine, on this day of mine, in this month of mine, in this year of mine, until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever abandons it during my lifetime or after my death, while having a just or unjust ruler, out of contempt for it and denial of it, let him know: Allah will not gather his affairs, and will not bless him in his affair. Beware, beware..."

Malik narrated from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever bathes on Friday and then goes in the third hour, it is as if he had offered a camel; whoever goes in the second hour, it is as if he had offered a cow; whoever goes in the third hour, it is as if he had offered a horned ram; whoever goes in the fourth hour, it is as if he had offered a hen; whoever goes in the fifth hour, it is as if he had offered an egg. When the imam begins [the sermon], the scrolls are folded up and the angels come to listen to the remembrance." He (al-Sam'ani) said, may Allah be pleased with him: Abu al-Husayn ibn al-Naqur informed us of this; Abu Tahir al-Mukhallis informed us; Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id informed us; Abu Mus'ab informed us from Malik, the report.

It is also related, through the narration of ʿImran ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever bathes on Friday, his sins and errors are washed away; when he goes, Allah records for every step the deed of twenty years; when the prayer is finished, he is rewarded with the deed of two hundred years." The report is very strange.

The third report: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever bathes on Friday from major impurity, puts on the best of his clothes, touches some of the perfume of his house, and does not separate two people (who are sitting together), will be forgiven what is between him and the next Friday, and three days more." Al-Bukhari mentioned it in his book.

It is also reported in some traditions that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever abandons the Friday prayer three times without an excuse, Allah will seal his heart." And Allah knows best.
